_page: The public homepage of Artosia at artosia.matsuokengo.com. Artosia is a free program for a church's media desk: it puts the words of songs, Bible verses and announcements on the projector during a service. It runs on a Windows computer. The reader is a church volunteer of any age who was sent the link and wants to know what this is and how to get it. Register: informal and warm, addressing the reader as kamu where a pronoun is needed. Plain, modest, concrete: say what the thing is and does, then stop. No exclamation marks, no em-dash, no en-dash, no middle dot, no emoji. Sentence case. Program names (Artosia, EasiSlides, OpenLyrics, PowerPoint, Windows, Wi-Fi, GPL-3.0-or-later, artosia.exe) stay as written. Names of things inside the program must be the words the program itself uses in Indonesian: look them up in docs/i18n/id.json (Design, Screens, Announcements, Search, Prev and Next, the plan, Preview and Live).

meta_title.where: the browser tab and the search engine result's blue line
meta_title.does: names the program, then says in a few words what kind of program it is (free, for worship services, shows words on a projector, for Windows). Starts with 'Artosia:'

meta_description.where: the grey text under a search engine result
meta_description.does: one or two sentences: Artosia puts song words, Bible verses and announcements on a church's projector; it is free, for Windows, and the program itself speaks Indonesian and English

nav_what.where: top bar link that jumps to the part of the page listing what the program does

nav_start.where: top bar link that jumps to the three steps for getting started
nav_start.does: names that part, one word if possible

nav_other_language.where: top bar link on the Indonesian page that opens the English page
nav_other_language.does: the name of the English language as English speakers write it

nav_download.where: small button at the right of the top bar; pressing it downloads the program

hero_title.where: the big headline, the first thing read
hero_title.does: says what the program does in one short sentence ending in a full stop: the words of the songs appear on the projector screen. Must fit two lines on a phone

hero_lead.where: one sentence under the headline, grey
hero_lead.does: says what Artosia is: free software that puts songs, Bible verses and announcements on a church's projector, run from the Windows computer at the media desk (where the multimedia volunteer sits)

download_button.where: the main black button; pressing it downloads the program
download_button.does: says the act and that it is for Windows

source_button.where: quiet outline button beside the main one; opens the page where the program's source code is public
source_button.does: names what it opens: the source code

release_note.where: small grey line under the download button
release_note.does: three facts separated by commas: the version, written as the word for version followed by the token {version}; the size, written as the token {size} followed by MB and the word zip; and that it is for Windows 10 and 11. Keep both tokens exactly

stage_prev.where: button under a picture of the program; steps the picture back one slide. It mirrors the program's own key for the previous slide
stage_prev.does: the program's own short word for going to the previous slide

stage_next.where: button under a picture of the program; steps the picture forward one slide. It mirrors the program's own key for the next slide
stage_next.does: the program's own short word for going to the next slide

stage_count.does: which picture of how many, using the tokens {n} and {of}, for example the Indonesian way of writing '2 of 4'. Keep both tokens exactly

stage_caption.where: one grey line beside the buttons, under the picture of the program's window
stage_caption.does: tells the reader to press the forward button (use the same word as stage_next), and that the row marked red is what the congregation sees on the projector

stage_alt_0.where: text read aloud by a screen reader in place of the first picture
stage_alt_0.does: describes it: the Artosia window, with the plan for the service on the left, the next song in the middle, and on the right the slide now on the projector, marked red

stage_alt_1.where: screen reader text for the second picture
stage_alt_1.does: the same window one slide later

stage_alt_2.where: screen reader text for the third picture
stage_alt_2.does: the same window two slides later

stage_alt_3.where: screen reader text for the fourth picture
stage_alt_3.does: the same window three slides later

what_title.where: heading of the part that shows what the program does, each with a picture
what_title.does: names the part, same idea as nav_what

wall_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the projector screen showing only four lines of a song
wall_title.does: the congregation sees nothing but the words

wall_text.does: the projector is run by a separate program of its own, so the words stay on the screen even if the operator's window stops working

wall_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
wall_caption.does: names what the picture is: the projector

wall_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
wall_alt.does: four lines of a song in white on a dark blue screen

search_title.where: small heading above a picture of the search box with songs found
search_title.does: a song can be found from any line of its words

search_text.where: one or two sentences under that heading
search_text.does: type the title or whatever line you remember; spelling mistakes are forgiven; the words that match are marked

search_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
search_caption.does: the search opens as soon as you start typing

search_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
search_alt.does: the search box with two words typed and four songs found, the matching words in blue

look_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the dialog where the look of the slides is chosen
look_title.does: you pick a look that is already made (you do not have to design one)

look_text.where: one or two sentences under that heading
look_text.does: six looks are ready; behind the words you can put a colour, a picture, a looping video or a camera; there are 318 free backgrounds to choose from

look_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
look_caption.does: the program's own Indonesian name for its Design dialog

look_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
look_alt.does: the Design dialog with six ready looks and a preview of the words

screens_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the dialog for projector screens, where four corners of the picture can be moved
screens_title.does: the crooked picture on the wall can be straightened without leaving the desk

screens_text.where: one or two sentences under that heading
screens_text.does: a second screen is found and filled automatically; you move its four corners until the picture on the wall is square

screens_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
screens_caption.does: the program's own Indonesian name for its Screens dialog

screens_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
screens_alt.does: the Screens dialog listing two screens, with four corners that can be moved

notices_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the announcements editor
notices_title.does: announcements shown before the service starts

notices_text.does: slides that repeat in a loop while people arrive; they can be typed in, or brought in from a PowerPoint file or from a list of birthdays

notices_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
notices_caption.does: the program's own Indonesian name for Announcements

notices_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
notices_alt.does: the announcements editor: a list of slides, and a birthdays slide shown in the small projector preview

start_title.where: heading of the part with three numbered steps to get the program running

step_download_title.where: step 1, bold word after the number
step_download_title.does: the act: download. Same word as nav_download

step_download_text.does: it is a single zip file of {size} MB. Keep the token exactly

step_unzip_title.where: step 2, bold word after the number
step_unzip_title.does: the act: unpack the zip file, the everyday Indonesian word for it

step_unzip_text.where: one or two short sentences under step 2
step_unzip_text.does: unpack it into a folder you are allowed to write to, for example Documents (use the folder's name as an Indonesian Windows shows it); the reason: Artosia updates its own files there

step_open_title.where: step 3, bold words after the number
step_open_title.does: the act: open the file artosia.exe

step_open_text.does: the first time, Windows may show a warning that it does not know the publisher; the reason is that the program files do not carry a paid code signature

facts_title.where: heading of the last part, a list of short facts
facts_title.does: things worth knowing before you download

fact_runs_text.does: three short facts: it is built for Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit; so far it has only been tried on Windows 11; versions for Mac and Linux are planned and have not been tested

fact_needs_text.does: a projector or a second screen; one screen alone is enough to try the program

fact_bible_term.does: the Bible, the common Indonesian word

fact_bible_text.does: verses are called up by their reference, with an example reference written the Indonesian way (book Yohanes, chapter 3, verses 16 to 18, with a hyphen), taken from the Bibles you add to the program

fact_library_term.does: the song collection you already have from an older program

fact_library_text.does: it reads song files from EasiSlides and OpenLyrics

fact_phone_term.does: a phone, the everyday Indonesian word

fact_phone_text.does: a web page opened on a phone on the same Wi-Fi can move the slides

fact_language_text.does: Indonesian and English, both in the program's window and in its search (Indonesian named first on this page)

fact_updates_text.does: every installed copy fetches the newest version by itself and checks its digital signature

fact_price_text.does: free; the source code is open under the licence GPL-3.0-or-later

footer_source.where: small footer link to the public source code

footer_releases.where: small footer link to the list of every released version

footer_licence.where: small footer link to the licence text
